notes: Create/Edit field rules: provider int; plan_name max 250; plan_code max 100; type in {1,2}; plan_type in {1,2,3}; billing_type in {1,2}; description max 255.
Login and Provider plan list use dxhub-dev-api host from collection; Plan CRUD uses dev-console-api.jpmob.jp from collection.
Detailed View URL was missing in the Postman item; GET /api/v1/plan/provider/{id} assumed—confirm with backend if different.

testCases.testCaseDescription: Verify that the Create Plan API returns success when all required fields are valid according to the schema.
testCases.testSteps:
1. Open API testing tool or automation environment.
2. Enter API endpoint: https://dev-console-api.jpmob.jp/api/v1/plan/provider.
3. Select HTTP method: POST.
4. Set request headers: Authorization: DXHUB <valid_token>; Content-Type: application/json; Accept: application/json.
5. Provide authentication token as per test (DXHUB <access_token> in Authorization header when required).
6. Enter request payload: {"provider":9,"plan_name":"ValidPlanName","plan_code":"VALID_CODE","type":1,"plan_type":1,"billing_type":1,"description":"Valid description"}
7. Send the API request.
8. Verify HTTP status code and response body against Expected Result.
testCases.preCondition: Valid API access token exists. Provider ID 9 (or a valid provider from environment) exists.
testCases.expectedResult: The API should return HTTP 201 or 200 with Content-Type application/json. The response should include the created plan identifier and persisted field values matching the request.

2. Enter API endpoint: https://dev-console-api.jpmob.jp/api/v1/plan/provider.
3. Select HTTP method: POST.
4. Set request headers: Authorization: DXHUB <valid_token>; Content-Type: application/json; Accept: application/json.
5. Provide authentication token as per test (DXHUB <access_token> in Authorization header when required).
6. Enter request payload: {"provider":9,"plan_name":"ValidPlanName","plan_code":"VALID_CODE","type":1,"plan_type":1,"billing_type":1,"description":null}
7. Send the API request.
8. Verify HTTP status code and response body against Expected Result.
testCases.expectedResult: The API should return HTTP 400 or 422 indicating description is invalid.

testCases.testCaseDescription: Verify that an error is returned when the Create Plan API is called without Authorization header.
testCases.testSteps:
1. Open API testing tool or automation environment.
2. Enter API endpoint: https://dev-console-api.jpmob.jp/api/v1/plan/provider.
3. Select HTTP method: POST.
4. Set Content-Type: application/json. Omit Authorization header.
5. Enter valid JSON body: {"provider":9,"plan_name":"ValidPlanName","plan_code":"VALID_CODE","type":1,"plan_type":1,"billing_type":1,"description":"Valid description"}.
6. Send the API request.
7. Verify response.
testCases.expectedResult: The API should return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

testCases.testCaseDescription: Verify that an error is returned when Content-Type is not application/json for the Create Plan API.
testCases.testSteps:
1. Open API testing tool or automation environment.
2. Enter API endpoint: https://dev-console-api.jpmob.jp/api/v1/plan/provider.
3. Select HTTP method: POST.
4. Set Authorization with valid token. Set Content-Type to text/plain (not application/json).
5. Send body as JSON string: {"provider":9,"plan_name":"ValidPlanName","plan_code":"VALID_CODE","type":1,"plan_type":1,"billing_type":1,"description":"Valid description"}.
6. Send the API request.
7. Verify response.
testCases.expectedResult: The API should return HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type or 400 as per implementation.
